name: PCW Northwest Wrestling (Episode 1)

date.source: the promotion's own first-card post, 8 February 1996

matches.finish: "5150" John Doe defeated Francis Quincy Cleveland with a heart punch ("Father Knows Best") in the opening round of the promotion's debut tournament.

The Warden and "Hollywood" Johnny Dreamer both had a shoulder down for a simultaneous three-count; the promotion's own referee ruled it a draw, with a ten-minute rematch ordered for the following week.

appearances.source: a videotaped promo aired mid-broadcast, boasting of titles held elsewhere ahead of his own debut tournament bout

notes: The promotion's debut broadcast, opening a tournament for its first title, the Pacific Heavyweight Belt. The bracket names eight further entrants for future rounds; none of their bouts survive in the held record, and the tournament's own outcome is not attested here, so they are not structured as appearances.

matches.title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-tag-team
matches.stipulation: PCW World Tag Team Championship Match
matches.finish: The Devil's Disciples retained against Crusher Tech when Chopper Davidson hit a top-rope legdrop (the "Chop Shop Drop") for the pin.
Hardcore Harris, debuting, dominated "Cool" Chris Courage from bell to bell.
Both men leapt from the top of the cage together; Ultimate Maniac was ruled to have touched down first at 11:19. The two shook hands afterward.
Johnny "Cool" Coles won on his return to the promotion; no further detail of the bout survives in the promotion's own account.
Sin & Salvation defeated Gangsta's Paradise when Caleb Temple submitted Nibs with the Last Rites, a Scorpion Deathlock.
Dr. D-Day defeated Kevin Jade with his finisher, the Landmine, after "Iron Man" Jack Kelly interfered against Jade at ringside.
Christian Kingsworth, debuting, won by countout after a ringside onlooker seized a chair intended for him and Iceman walked to the back rather than continue.

matches.title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-television
matches.finish: Thorn retained against "Master Of Pain" Barry Hart with a bridging back suplex, punishing a moment of ring-apron showboating.

appearances.source: interfered against Kevin Jade at ringside during the Dr. D-Day match

matches.title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-columbia-valley
matches.finish: Drago retained against The Prophet in 34:13.

appearances.source: a backstage interview previewing Crusher Tech's own title challenge against ASSpocalypse '97, elsewhere on the same joint card
a backstage interview previewing Crusher Tech's own title challenge against ASSpocalypse '97, elsewhere on the same joint card

notes: A joint New Year's pay-per-view with the EWA and DPW; only the promotion's own Columbia Valley title portion is structured here. The card's other billed PCW segments — a Tag Team Championship challenge and a "Luck of the Draw" gimmick match — are collected but their results are not preserved clearly enough in the held record to structure.

matches.stipulation: PCW Columbia Valley Championship Match, Falls Count Anywhere

appearances.source: billed by the promotion's own later broadcasts and a rival federation's contemporaneous interview as the wrestler crowned in this card's 32-man Bunkhouse Brawl for the vacant World Heavyweight Championship
credited on-air, in commentary during the Bunkhouse Brawl, as the new PCW World Tag Team Champions

notes: A capture defect strikes this card hard: five of its eight surviving parts end mid-sentence, spliced onto an unrelated Google Groups thread listing. The World Heavyweight Bunkhouse Brawl's own winner and the Television Championship challenge earlier on the card are both casualties of that defect and are not structured as matches here; both title outcomes are instead recorded on their own title's reign history from the promotion's later billing.

matches.title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-tag-team
matches.stipulation: PCW/DPW World Tag Team Title Unification Match
matches.finish: Bigger Than Hollywood, the promotion's own Tag Team Champions, defeated DPW's own champions Negaforce (Adams pinning Malachite off a Reverse DDT) to unify the two belts.

matches.title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-world-heavyweight
matches.stipulation: PCW World Heavyweight Championship Match, Texas Death Match — winner becomes Unified World Champion
matches.finish: Gunnar "The Grizzly" Gaines retained in 35 minutes, becoming PCW's Unified World Heavyweight Champion.

matches.title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-world-heavyweight
matches.finish: "Hardcore" Matt Harris pinned Captain Midnight with the Hardcore Cutter to become new champion, in a match restarted once already after Midnight refused an earlier disqualification win over Harris. Steve Sampson attacked Harris after the bell.

matches.title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-columbia-valley
matches.finish: Ruled a No Contest after Thorn led challenger "American Nightmare" Gary Grayson to the ring already carrying the physical title belt; The Extremist retained and had the belt returned to him.

matches.title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-tag-team
matches.stipulation: PCW World Tag Team Championship Match, Caged Elimination
matches.finish: Crusher Tech regained the (unified) title from Bigger Than Hollywood in 45:13.

matches.title: pcw-grapplearium-1996-television
matches.finish: "Maniac" Joe Colosi retained against Dimension in 11:07.
